chunks: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever has a pregnant wife and intends to name [the child] Muhammad or Ali, a boy will be born for him.'

key_terms.حَمْل: pregnancy; in classical Arabic, can refer both to the act of carrying and to the fetus/child being carried
key_terms.رَفَعَهُ: elevated [the chain]; a marfu' hadith is one where an intermediate narrator attributes it directly to the Prophet without naming all links
key_terms.غُلَام: a boy; in classical Arabic refers specifically to a male child or youth
key_terms.نَوَى: made the intention (niyya); intentionality is a foundational concept in Islamic practice — the inner resolve to act
key_terms.يُسَمِّي: to name; the act of naming (tasmiya) is a recognized sunnah act performed after birth

ai.seo_question: Does naming a child Muhammad or Ali before birth guarantee the birth of a boy according to hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith records a prophetic saying attributed to the Prophet Muhammad through a marfu' (elevated) chain via Sahl ibn Ziyad. The Prophet declares that when a man whose wife is pregnant makes the sincere intention to name the child Muhammad or Ali — the two most blessed names in the Shia tradition — God will bless him with a male child. This narration reflects the spiritual significance attributed to the names of the Prophet and the first Imam, and the belief that righteous intentions, particularly those connected to the Ahl al-Bayt, carry divine blessing.
